_readme: Case-study areas as swappable configurations (build spec §4). One ships: Panjim / Mandovi. The CRZ facts (areas, source, policy notes) are read directly from data/source/panjim_mandovi_case_study.json. The class grid comes from src/data/panjimCrzGrid.json, built by tools/build_crz_grid.py. What lives here is the analytic set-up: how the coastline is divided into segments, and which grid classes act as hazard sources. Segment boundaries are an analytic choice made in this build, drawn along named reaches of the real coastline, not official boundaries.

areas.name: Panjim (Panaji), Goa: city and its same-bank Mandovi, Aguada Bay and Zuari frontage

hinterlandBandKm.note: Land within this distance of a segment's shoreline (measured over land) counts as that segment's exposed hinterland. Analytic choice: twice the 500 m landward extent of CRZ regulation from the HTL, to catch khazan lands along the creeks behind the CRZ strip.

mangroveBandKm.note: Existing mangrove belt width = mangrove area within this distance of the shoreline ÷ shoreline length. A crude average across the segment; a transect survey resolves it.

dividingLine.note: A line drawn down the middle of the Mandovi channel and Aguada Bay. Shore cells north of it belong to the Bardez (north-bank) side, cells south of it to the Tiswadi (Panjim) side.

flowConnectors.note: Hydraulic connections narrower than one grid cell, added by hand so water can travel along them. The Nerul creek's outlet to the Mandovi mouth does not survive the ~55 m classification: the creek ends inland on the grid, so without this connector the creek would receive no hazard at all. The connector's exact line is approximate (analytic choice, reasoned_extrapolation); replace it with the surveyed channel when available.

segments.name: Miramar–Caranzalem beach
segments.description: Panjim's west-facing sandy beach on Aguada Bay: CRZ-II urban frontage.
segments.settingNote: Grid: shore median 3.1 km from open sea (CRZ-IVA) → open coast; khazan 0.04 km² (below the 0.1 km² rule). Hand check: Miramar–Caranzalem is a sandy beach (segment description; Esri imagery).

segments.name: Panjim city riverfront (Campal–Patto)
segments.description: The city's Mandovi frontage along D.B. Marg: dense CRZ-II urban land, the ferry and casino waterfront.
segments.settingNote: Grid: shore median 7.0 km from open sea → channel; mangrove belt 54 m (< 75 m) → estuary bank, not creek; khazan 0.53 km² → khazan present. Hand check: the Mandovi frontage along D.B. Marg (estuary bank), with khazan fields in the hinterland band.

segments.name: St Inez creek, Ribandar and Merces belt
segments.description: The south-bank belt east of the city: CRZ-IA mangroves and khazan fields along the St Inez / Ourem creeks and the Ribandar causeway.
segments.settingNote: Grid: shore median 9.4 km from open sea → channel; mangrove belt 98 m (≥ 75 m) with khazan 1.03 km² → creek; khazan present. Hand check: St Inez / Ourem creeks lined with mangrove and khazan (segment description); the segment also includes the Ribandar Mandovi bank.

segments.name: Dona Paula headland and Zuari-facing shore
segments.description: Rocky Dona Paula headland and the Vainguinim–Bambolim shore facing the Zuari mouth.
segments.settingNote: Grid: shore median 2.3 km from open sea → open coast; khazan 0.05 km² (below the rule). The grid cannot tell rock from sand. Hand check: the Dona Paula headland is rocky (segment description). The segment also includes the sandy Vainguinim pocket beach, which this one-setting-per-segment rule does not capture.

excludedAreas.name: South-east corner (Zuari-side salt pans and khazans, ~73.86–73.90 E, 15.45–15.48 N)
excludedAreas.reason: Drains to the Zuari, whose channel lies mostly outside this window, so the window has no hazard source for it. It is excluded from Phase 1 segments rather than assigned a made-up hazard.

existingMeasuresPolicy.mangroves: Where the grid shows CRZ-IA mangrove fringing a segment's shoreline, the baseline includes a mangrove belt of the measured average width. Mature stands are assumed (maturity 1.0, reasoned_extrapolation).
existingMeasuresPolicy.khazan: Where the grid shows khazan land in a segment's hinterland, the baseline includes a tidal-wetland/polder unit of that area. Following the source file's policy note, bund and sluice-gate infrastructure marked 'prior to 1991' on the CZMP counts as CURRENT existing infrastructure. Bund/sluice locations are not yet extracted, and the khazan area is a placeholder_needs_calibration estimate, so the baseline khazan storage is a placeholder too.
existingMeasuresPolicy.engineered: No existing engineered structures (seawalls, embankments, breakwaters) are in the source data, so none are in the baseline. Known structures, such as the Panjim riverfront embankment, can be added in a scenario.

scope.note: Scope set by the user (STEP_PROMPT, 2026-09-25): Panjim and the frontage directly touching it on the same bank only. Nothing across the Mandovi, and nothing up the Bardez coast. The hazard model still runs on the full CRZ window, because storm surge enters through the river mouth and the river flood arrives from upstream; the map and all results cover only the Panjim scope.

droppedSegments.reason: Out of scope: across the Mandovi or up the Bardez coast, not Panjim (user instruction, 2026-09-25).

droppedSegments.reason: Out of scope: across the Mandovi or up the Bardez coast, not Panjim (user instruction, 2026-09-25).

areas._readme_note: Segments were narrowed from nine to four on 2026-09-25; see scope and droppedSegments.

population.coverage: Panaji (M Corp. + OG): the Corporation of the City of Panaji (40,017) plus its out-growth, including Taleigao (24,201); 37 listed wards and units.
population.allocation: Each segment receives total × (its hinterland land area ÷ all in-scope land area). In-scope land outside the four 1 km hinterland bands keeps its share, so the segments sum to less than the total.
population.note: A real census total distributed by an area-weighted split, not ward-verified: population density is not uniform, the census unit's boundary does not match the tool's scope, and 2011 is 15 years old. Ward-level geography (37 units, available in the source) would allow a better allocation.

rescale.label: GHS-POP rescaled to the Census 2011 towns

growthFactor.label: Population growth since the 2011 census
growthFactor.note: Kept at 1.0 (no growth): no checked source for the growth of these towns since 2011 was reachable in this pass. The MoHFW Technical Group's population projections for 2011-2036 (state level) or a 2021+ town count would set it.

rescale.note: Audit A8 (Phase 3). GHS-POP places a taluk-level total where the built-up volume is, about 1.6x the census towns' 2011 count. People on khazan-mask and CRZ-IA mangrove cells are set to zero (nobody lives in the paddy or the mangrove), then the people in each census town's cells (DataMeet 2001 boundaries, by cell centre) are scaled so they sum to its Census 2011 total x the growth factor x the share of the town's GHS-POP inside the grid window (tools/build_pop_grid.mjs). Panaji and Bambolim are scaled together: DataMeet's Bambolim polygon covers Patto, part of Panaji city, so scaling it alone would give Patto Bambolim's small census count (6,885 people for 25,203 GHS-POP people). Cells outside the four towns (Curca and slivers) are only zeroed on khazan and mangrove, not scaled.

settingRules.note: Segment settings are derived from the CRZ grid by three rules, then confirmed by hand: (1) open coast if the median distance from the segment's shore cells to open sea (CRZ-IVA) is ≤ 4 km, otherwise a channel; (2) a channel segment is a creek if its mangrove belt is ≥ 75 m wide and it has ≥ 0.1 km² of khazan, otherwise an estuary bank; (3) khazan is present if the hinterland band holds ≥ 0.1 km² of khazan. Sandy vs rocky open coast cannot be read from the grid and is set by hand from the segment descriptions. Thresholds are this tool's choices, not literature values.

rain.note: Creek catchments for 'Heavy rain at high tide' (audit M15). Each catchment drains to its outlets: the tidal creeks and Mala lake as mapped in OpenStreetMap (way ids below, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL, fetched 23 Oct 2026), or, for central Panjim, the Mandovi water cells along the riverfront. Every in-scope land cell is given to the outlet it drains to by a priority-flood over the DEM (lowest spill path), so the catchment boundaries are the DEM's ridges: Altinho drains north to central Panjim, east to Mala and Ourem, and west to St Inez. The creeks are narrower than a grid cell and are not water in the CRZ grid, so their lines are drawn in as outlets. Only these four catchments are modelled; other land drains straight to the sea or river and is not counted.

catchments.name: St Inez creek (Tonca, St Inez, Campal)

existingMeasures.derivedNote: Mala flood-water pumping station (inaugurated 5 Jul 2023): five generator pumps, 3 x 300 HP + 2 x 60 HP = 1020 HP (Gomantak Times, 22 Jun 2023). Capacity = pump efficiency 0.75 x 761 kW / (water density x g x 5 m lift) = 11.6 m3/s. Placeholder: the lift and efficiency are assumed (a 3-8 m lift gives 7-19 m3/s); no design discharge was found.

Mala lake used as the retention basin for the Altinho catchment (Goa DIP press release, 5 Jul 2023; Gomantak Times, 22 Jun 2023). Volume = lake area 16,200 m2 (OpenStreetMap way 89208031) x 1.5 m usable depth = 24,000 m3. Placeholder: the usable depth is assumed.
Two electrically operated actuator gates close at high tide to keep Ourem creek water out of Mala (Goa DIP press release, 5 Jul 2023). Reasoned: reported in the press, not seen in a design.

subCatchmentKm2.label: Largest outlet sub-catchment
subCatchmentKm2.note: Audit A4 (Phase 3): the rain that reaches a creek or the river ponds near where it reached it, not across the whole catchment. The outlet cells along each creek line (or along the Mandovi bank for central Panjim) are grouped in order into sub-catchments of at most about 1 km² of contributing land (the brief's size). A modelling choice, not a measured drain network: OSM maps only 6 drains in the window, too few to cut the catchments at real outfalls. Replace with the storm-drain network and its outfalls (CCP / Imagine Panaji).

fieldBunds.label: Field bunds outside the CZMP khazan mask (Patto, Taleigao, St Inez / Merces)
fieldBunds.note: Ferdin (23 Oct 2026): the Patto and Taleigao fields are bunded, like the khazan in the CZMP mask, and so are the St Inez / Merces fields east of 73.848 E. The bunds themselves are not mapped, so the fields are traced from data (tools/trace_field_bunds.py, see trace): open, unbuilt, low land inside the three named areas (Cowork's two test boxes, docs/STEP_PROMPT_model_p3_accuracy.md, and the St Inez / Merces area east of 73.848 E to the St Inez segment's edge, 73.875 E), from Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 (smooth, green surface), the OSM + Microsoft building footprints (under 10% of the cell roofed) and OSM farmland. Built-up low land, such as Patto Plaza and the bus-stand blocks, is left out: a field bund does not protect it. Inside the traced fields, every in-scope cell that is unclassified land, CRZ-III or a waterbody, outside the khazan mask, with ground at or below spring high water (+1.0 m), joins the khazan land behind the bunds: the same crest (bundCrestM, 1.5 m, 1.0-2.0 m placeholder) and the same bund-failure toggle. Extent: reasoned_extrapolation (traced at the 55 m grid, not surveyed); crest: placeholder_needs_calibration.

trace.method: tools/trace_field_bunds.py: open, unbuilt, low land inside the Patto, Taleigao and St Inez / Merces areas (fieldBunds.boxes), as connected groups of grid cells. Field cell: unclassified, CRZ-III or waterbody, outside the khazan mask, more than 3 cells from the open sea and east of 73.815 E (the Miramar beach strip), ground at or below the bund crest (1.5 m), roof footprint under 10% of the cell (OSM + Microsoft), and in Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 a smooth (brightness std <= 10 of 255), green (green >= red) and not bright (mean <= 100) surface, or OSM landuse=farmland/paddy. Groups of at least 3 cells. Rings are read even-odd (holes are unbuilt patches that fail the rule). The model bunds only the cells at or below spring high water.
